title: Bare MADR deprecation stays visible unless a successor proves closure
context: MADR allows a deprecated lifecycle without naming a replacement. Treating that word alone as superseded fabricated a lifecycle edge, closed valid time at the record date, and silently removed the imported decision from current recall.
decision: Import a bare deprecated ADR as an accepted advisory record, retain the raw source lifecycle in provenance evidence, and emit a deterministic review warning. Only an explicit successor relation may map deprecated to superseded and close valid_to at the successor date.
consequences: Bare deprecated records remain visible for review instead of disappearing as invented history.
Deprecated by ADR-N still derives both supersession pointers and closes the historical window at the successor date.
No Decision schema migration is required; imported:madr provenance remains advisory and preserves the raw status.
alternatives_rejected: Map every deprecated status to superseded: this invents a replacement edge and can silently drop a record with no successor.
Add a new deprecated Decision status: this requires a cross-cutting schema and query migration for an import-only distinction that provenance and a warning can preserve.
Map deprecated to rejected or proposed: either rewrites the source meaning or unnecessarily removes an otherwise accepted historical choice from normal current recall.
